'''Sergei Vasilyevich Kerov''' (Russian: Сергей Васильевич Керов; born 21 June 1946 in [[Leningrad]] died 30 July 2000) was a Russian [[mathematician]] and university professor. His research included [[operator algebra|operator algebras]], [[combinatorics]], [[probability theory|probability]] and [[representation theory]].<ref name="StPeterburgMathSoc">{{cite web |url=http://www.mathsoc.spb.ru/pers/kerov/biograph.html |title= Brief Biography of Sergei Kerov |website= mathsoc.spb.ru|publisher=St. Petersburg Mathematical Society|access-date=2022-11-19}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|publisher=St. Petersburg Department of Steklov Mathematical Institute|url=http://www.pdmi.ras.ru/ru/institut/staff_LOMI.php|website=www.pdmi.ras.ru|title=Научные сотрудники ЛОМИ / ПОМИ прошлых лет|access-date=2022-11-19}}</ref>

== Life ==
Kerov was born in 1946 in [[Leningrad]] (now St. Petersburg). His father Vasily Kerov was a teacher for [[analytical chemistry]] at a university in Leningrad and his mother Marianna Nikolayeva was an expert in [[plant physiology|seed physiology]].<ref name="StPeterburgMathSoc" />

Kerov studied at the [[Saint Petersburg State University]]. He obtained a PhD in 1975 under the supervision of [[Anatoly Vershik]]. He was then a professor at various universities in St. Petersburg, including the [[Herzen State Pedagogical University|Herzen Pedagogical University]] and the University of Saint Petersburg. From 1993 he did research at the [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]] in St. Petersburg. In 1994 he received a [[Doctor of Sciences|Sc.D. (Doctor of Science)]] from the Steklov Institute for his work ''Asymptotic Representation Theory of the Symmetric Group, with Applications to Analysis''. From 1995 he was a professor at the University of Saint Petersburg.<ref name="StPeterburgMathSoc" />

In 2000 he died of a [[brain tumor]].<ref name="StPeterburgMathSoc" />

== Work ==

A list of Kerov's scientific articles was published in the Journal of Mathematical Sciences.<ref>{{cite journal|title=List of Publications of Sergei Kerov|journal=Journal of Mathematical Sciences|volume=121|number=3|pages=2300–2302|year=2004|doi=10.1023/B:JOTH.0000024610.98657.ac|publisher=Springer|s2cid=189866581 }}</ref>

In 1977 he proved together with [[Anatoly Vershik]] a limit theorem for the [[Plancherel measure]] for the [[symmetric group]] with a limiting shape which is now called ''Vershik–Kerov curve''.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=A.M. Vershik |author1-link=Anatoly Vershik|author2=S.V. Kerov |title=Asymptotics of the Plancherel measure of the symmetric group and the limiting shape of Young tableaux|journal=Soviet Math. Dokl.|volume=18|year=1977|pages=527–531}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Borodin, Alexei|author1-link=Alexei Borodin |author2=Andrei Okounkov |author2-link=Andrei Okounkov |author3=Grigori Olshanski |title=Asymptotics of Plancherel Measures for Symmetric Groups|journal=Journal of the American Mathematical Society|volume=13|number=3 |year=2000|pages=481–515|doi=10.1090/S0894-0347-00-00337-4 |jstor=2646116|s2cid=14183320 |doi-access=free}}</ref> The same result was also independently proved by Logan and Shepp and thus is also called ''Logan–Shepp curve''. The result was later improved by Kerov to a central limit theorem.<ref>{{cite conference|author1=Vladimir Ivanov |author2= Grigori Olshanski|chapter=Kerov's Central Limit Theorem for the Plancherel Measure on Young Diagrams |title=Symmetric Functions 2001: Surveys of Developments and Perspectives|conference=Proceedings of the NATO Advanced Study Institute on Symmetric Functions 2001: Surveys of Developments and Perspectives Cambridge, U.K. 25 June–6 July 2001|pages=93–151|publisher=Springer|year=2002|doi=10.1007/978-94-010-0524-1_3 |isbn=978-1-4020-0774-3 |s2cid=9763630  |editor=Sergey Fomin |editor-link=Sergey Fomin|series=NATO Science Series II: Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, vol. 74 |arxiv=math/0304010}}</ref>
